@graph.headline: Curbside vs inside vs white-glove delivery: what to confirm before you book

itemListElement.name: Curbside vs inside vs white-glove delivery: what to confirm before you book

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes — and only when it is agreed. FreightRight's knowledge base lists assembly among the things white-glove service may include, and is explicit that the scope depends on the carrier and the service agreement, so it has to be confirmed before booking (1). On our side the answer is plain: assembly and installation are not part of our published final-mile scope (5).

Often at the white-glove tier, but it should still be confirmed before booking (1) — and confirm what the words cover. Removing the delivered item's own packaging is one service; hauling away the old item it replaces is another, and the second is not implied by the first. Our published practice covers the delivered item's packaging (5); haul-away of old items is not published as part of our service.

mainEntity.name: Is debris removal included with a delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — appointment-based delivery is the norm for freight of any size. White-glove services commonly run on scheduled appointment windows (1), and retail freight deliveries are typically arranged on an appointment with a signature required (4). Our deliveries are arranged by appointment too; we publish no fixed window length — the appointment is set when the job is scoped and quoted (5).

mainEntity.name: Can a final-mile delivery be scheduled?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. FreightRight notes white-glove service is frequently used for residential freight shipments — furniture, appliances, electronics, medical equipment and other big or high-value pieces (1). Our final-mile deliveries run to homes as well as to offices, industrial sites and retail spaces, dispatched from the Winchester and Martinsburg branches (5). A residence with stairs or a heavy piece is exactly the delivery to confirm in detail before the day.

mainEntity.name: Is white-glove delivery available for residences?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the service is different work, not a different label. White-glove pricing carries two-person teams, the scheduling coordination of an appointment, the extra time to carry, place, unpack and inspect, and the liability management of handling heavy or high-value freight inside the building (1). A curbside price stops at the curb — and hands you the carry, the placement and the stair risk.

mainEntity.name: Why does white-glove delivery cost more than curbside?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check the item in its final position before the paperwork is signed: finish, corners, doors and drawers, and whether it is complete. Note any damage on the delivery documents, not after the crew has gone. Federal consumer guidance for household-goods moves is built on the same record — your rights if goods arrive lost or damaged run from what is documented at delivery (2). Our crews verify condition with you before they leave (5).
